exposure: Gestational age at birth (<32 weeks vs. >=32 weeks)
cohort: Premature newborns in Santiago de Cali, Colombia, from 2017 to 2019
finding: Poor prenatal care, maternal residence outside of Cali, Afro-ethnicity, and cesarean birth were associated with prematurity of less than 32 weeks, while lower birth weight, cesarean delivery, and a lower Apgar score at 5 minutes were associated with increased mortality.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with an increased risk of prematurity of less than 32 weeks and neonatal mortality.
